title: Some Desert Rats Never Drink Water, Ever (Here's Where It Comes From)
subject: kangaroo rat

scenes.text: Some desert rats never take a single sip of water. Ever.
The kangaroo rat eats dry seeds. Nothing else. No puddles, no dew, no water hole.
So where does the water come from? From the seeds themselves. Digesting them makes water inside its body.
It wastes almost none. Its urine is extremely concentrated, and its nose saves moisture from every breath.
It even slows its metabolism to cut the water that escapes through its skin.
Dinner is the drink. And when danger comes, it leaps about eight feet.

description:
Merriam's kangaroo rat can live its whole life without drinking water.
It makes water from dry seeds, and its kidneys and nose waste almost none.
Could you live on dry seeds in a desert?
first_comment: A desert rat that never drinks. What animal record should we cover next?
